headline: Champlain Housing Trust withdrew its Final Subdivision Plan application for the Armory.
summary: Members discussed the draft Economic Vitality section of the Winooski Comprehensive Plan and removed the word "evaluate" from one objective. Staff reported that Champlain Housing Trust withdrew its Final Subdivision Plan application for the Armory. Members unanimously approved the previous meeting minutes.
decisions: Approved the previous meeting minutes unanimously, 5-0.
Removed the word "evaluate" from objective #4 on vacant properties in the draft Economic Vitality section.
Champlain Housing Trust withdrew its Final Subdivision Plan application for the Armory.

plain_text:
10/8/2026 - Minutes
Call to Order
Members Present: John Baker, Vice Chair; Brian Colombini; Ruby Tetrick; Trevor Thomas; 
James Paradissis
City Staff Present: Ravi Venkataraman, Director of City Planning
Guests Present: Thomas Renner, Mayor; Bryn Oakleaf; Eli Ogilvie
Call to Order by: John
Meeting Start Time: 6:31 pm
Minutes Recorded by: Ravi
Changes to the Agenda
None
Public Comment
None
Approve Previous Meeting Minutes
Motion by: Ruby
Second: Brian
Decision: Unanimous. Motion carried
Discussion: Winooski Comprehensive Plan – The draft Economic Vitality section
Ravi gave an overview of the section and the materials provided. Brian asked about the term 
“economic vitality” and recommended a more accessible term. Ravi said that other municipal 
plans refer to this section as “economic development” or “economy”. John and Brian agreed on 
the term “economy” and keeping the introductory text on the section. Ruby asked about how the 
interconnections between the economy section and the other sections will be explained. Ravi 
said that the Safe, Healthy and Connected People Commission suggested a diagram showing 
the interconnections between the sections, and that he can add text that explains the 
connections between sections in the beginning of the Comprehensive Plan text.
Ravi reviewed the key issues subsection. Trevor said he appreciated the listing of a grocery 
store in the first bullet point and asked how the Planning Commission can work to advance this 
issue. Ravi said that further conversations may be needed if and when someone looks to open a 
grocery store in the City. Brian highlighted the mention of wayfinding in the 2019 plan which is 
still needed today, and the need for more accessible information about businesses and services 
in town, including bus service to Shaws in Colchester. Ravi said that the City had worked on 
wayfinding in 2019, that the work had petered out, and that further conversations with City 
Council are needed on the subject.
Ravi reviewed the draft goals and actions. Trevor underscored the need for consistency with the 
usage of terms. Trevor said that economic diversification should be added. The commission 
discussed the usage of the term “evaluate” and concluded to remove “evaluate” from objective 
#4 regarding vacant properties. John suggested more language on community spaces and 
parks. Ravi said another objective could be added on this to speak to establishing a sense of 
place.
Ravi reviewed the statistics included in this draft. Brian asked about data on informal labor in 
Winooski. Ravi said that he doesn’t have any granular data on Winooski that is also accurate. 
John asked if the goals should include getting more granular data on Winooski’s demographics. 
Brian suggested that this may be under the possible economic development director’s purview, 
and that to get more specific data would require more staff capacity. Eli suggested including 
data from similarly sized municipalities in Vermont as reference points. Ravi said that he has 
seen other municipal plans compare local option tax revenue across different municipalities, and 
said that could be included. John suggested including a comparison of municipalities based on a 
per capita number of establishments.
John asked about representation in the feedback received for the comprehensive plan so far. 
Ravi said that outreach is still ongoing, and that he is being mindful of projects the City has done 
in the recent past and is currently doing to make sure he isn’t asking the same questions to the 
community.
Discussion: Section 248a Notice – 31 East Spring St
Ravi gave an overview of the proposed project. Ravi said that this is a required notification to the 
Planning Commission and that if the Planning Commission has any comments, they can 
provide comments to the state Public Utility Commission directly. Ravi said that the Local 
Resources Advisory Board was given the opportunity to comment before the application was 
submitted to the state Public Utility Commission. Ravi said that the building already has a cell 
tower and that this proposal would add another tower next to the existing one. John said that the 
elevation drawings appear skewed.
City Updates
Updates from the Mayor
Thomas reviewed discussions from the previous City Council meeting, which 
included the tax the rich campaign, and the City budget.
Updates from the Inclusion and Belonging Commission
None
Updates from City Staff
Ravi said that Champlain Housing Trust has withdrawn their Final Subdivision Plan 
application for the Armory that was warned for the September Development Review 
Board meeting. Ravi reviewed the upcoming tentative Development Review Board 
meeting agenda. Ravi said that the number of zoning permit applications have been 
comparatively down in recent months.
Other Business
Adjourn
Motion by: Ruby
Second: Trevor
Meeting End Time: 7:30 pm
